grounds: Osteoarthritis of knee was first diagnosed on 2026-03-24, AFTER the policy start date 2024-01-21; by definition it is not a Pre-Existing Disease, so the waiting period does not apply.
letter:
Subject: Appeal Against Denial of Claim e29c9390-f9d2-4a4b-bda6-2493c1618d8e – Pre‑Existing Disease Waiting Period

Claim Details:  
Claim ID: e29c9390-f9d2-4a4b-bda6-2493c1618d8e  
Patient: Simran Reddy (Patient ID: 1a0f0ba8-b9c8-4143-917b-738370e9df5b)  
Date of Service: 2026-03-24  
Plan: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Plan Code: SGH‑SILVER) – Coverage effective from 2024-01-21  
Diagnosis: Osteoarthritis of knee (first diagnosed on 2026-03-24)  
Procedure: Physical therapy procedure (Orthopedic category)  
Claim Amount: INR 24,563.43  
[suraksha_silver_policy#5]

Grounds for Appeal:  
The insurer’s denial cites a pre‑existing disease waiting period. Under the policy definition, a Pre‑Existing Disease is any condition diagnosed or treated within 48 months prior to the first policy start date. Osteoarthritis of the knee was first diagnosed on 2026-03-24, which is after the policy start date of 2024-01-21. Consequently, it does not meet the definition of a Pre‑Existing Disease, and the waiting period in Clause 4.2 is inapplicable. This interpretation is directly supported by the policy wording. [suraksha_silver_policy#5] [suraksha_silver_policy#11]

Clinical Necessity:  
The treating orthopaedic specialist has determined that physical therapy is medically necessary for the management of the patient’s newly diagnosed osteoarthritis of the knee. The doctor will attach detailed clinical notes and treatment justification to substantiate the necessity of the procedure. [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]

Reference to Denial Standards:  
According to the insurer’s own denial standards, the burden of proof for applying a pre‑existing disease exclusion rests with the insurer, which must provide documentary evidence that the condition existed before the policy start date. No such evidence has been presented. The insurer therefore has not satisfied the required burden of proof. [claims_procedure_and_grievance#6]

Specific Request:  
In light of the above, we request that the denial be withdrawn, the claim be re‑processed, and the amount of INR 24,563.43 be paid in full under the terms of the Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan. [suraksha_silver_policy#5]

Thank you for your prompt attention to this matter.

Insurance Desk (on behalf of the treating provider)

citations.section: Suraksha Silver Individual Health Plan (Policy Wording) > 4. Waiting Periods > 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
citations.quote:
### 4.2 Pre-Existing Disease Waiting Period
Expenses related to a Pre-Existing Disease (as defined in Clause 2.2) are covered only after 36 months of continuous coverage from the first policy start date. This waiting period applies ONLY to conditions meeting the definition in Clause 2.2.

citations.section: Claims Procedure, Denial Standards and Grievance Redressal > C3. Standards for Denial > C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
citations.quote:
### C3.2 Burden of Proof for Exclusions and Waiting Periods
The insurer bears the burden of proving that an exclusion or waiting period applies. For a Pre-Existing Disease denial, the insurer must show documentary evidence that the condition was diagnosed or treated before the policy start date.
